gateStability.assertion: graphEmpty: at least one drawn frame, zero painted pixels, and every pixel equal to the engine clear colour
gateStability.stabilityRunsNote: 20 consecutive standalone runs of the gate, all PASS, every one reporting mapFrames 2 and mapBackground 521550 of 521550. They were executed on the working tree whose two changed files are byte-identical to those committed in 5cd1134d, immediately before that commit; the gate then passed again as part of this receipt's gate sequence.
gateStability.previousBehaviour: On db073ce4 the same gate failed 2 of 12 runs, always reporting the full 915x570 canvas as painted.
gateStability.rootCause: The empty-scope probe read the map canvas in a task that could precede the engine's requestAnimationFrame draw, and ResizeObserver's initial callback reassigned canvas.width/height, which reallocates the WebGL drawing buffer even when the size is unchanged. An uncleared buffer reads back as transparent black, which is not the clear colour, so every pixel was classified as painted.
gateStability.fix: ui/public/graph-engine.mjs gained renderNow(), a synchronous draw that cancels any queued frame, plus a frame counter, and resize() now reallocates only on a real size change. scripts/web-ui-browser-e2e.mjs forces a frame through renderNow() before reading pixels and asserts a drawn frame with every pixel equal to the clear colour, so a never-cleared buffer can no longer be mistaken for a painted one.
gateStability.notWeakened: The assertion was tightened, not relaxed: the old check only required zero painted pixels, which an uncleared canvas could never satisfy but a blank one could have. No retry-until-pass was added.
gateStability.engineChangeJustification: The probe cannot reach the engine otherwise: the KnowledgeGraph instance is a module-local binding in ui/public/pages/graph.mjs, and only the engine can draw synchronously. The engine already drew synchronously for exportPNG(), so renderNow() exposes an existing capability; the resize() guard also removes a real product defect that blanked an already-drawn map on every no-op ResizeObserver callback.

releaseConclusion: All thirteen gates PASS on the clean final v0.5.0 candidate 5cd1134d, each on its first attempt: typecheck, a build that reproduced the tracked dist/, 98 files / 1015 Vitest tests, 26 Codex slices, 105 total slices, installer, marketplace, packaged runtime (memex-0.5.0.tgz, 311 files, 9 MCP tools), offline lifecycle 9/9, the real-Chrome Memex Workspace E2E (10 check groups, 0 runtime errors), 82 Workspace unit tests, isolated plugin validation (11 substitute checks, matching 0.5.0 plugin and MCP server versions) and the benchmark contract. The graph readback flake recorded in the superseded db073ce4 receipt, which failed 2 of 12 runs, was fixed at its source rather than retried: the engine now offers a synchronous renderNow() and stops reallocating the drawing buffer on no-op resizes, and the probe forces a real frame and asserts every pixel equals the clear colour, a strictly stronger assertion than before. 20 consecutive standalone runs passed with identical pixel counts, recorded as stabilityRuns 20/20, and the opt-in --screenshots pass was confirmed to still produce its five captures. The full acceptance benchmark was NOT re-run: it is referenced as prior evidence measured on 236d7362 (PASS, 6/6 AC_PERF groups, knowledge map through `loopback HTTP /api/v2/graph` with 50 nodes and 49 edges on the native LOCAL WEBGL renderer), and the contract gate confirms that report still satisfies the committed contract; because this SHA touches the graph engine the benchmark's browser numbers are inherited rather than re-measured. Live user data, an authenticated Codex tier run, the formal plugin validator, benchmark numbers for this exact SHA, real-world performance, model quality and the accuracy of the README prose and screenshots are NOT_PROVEN.
